title: Intermittent composition across time is a strobed chain's composition, and in linear chains it is arrival
subject: When composition of two contacts across time, holding at some lags but not all, is fixed by the chain itself
conclusion: In a chain of three rings the lags at which the far contact binds the end rings recur with the period P of the chain's T-step maps, so a chain observed at one residue modulo P composes at every observed lag or at none: intermittent composition is a strobed chain's composition, whose phase the chain does not fix. For linear or affine rules with affine contact laws the composing lags are exactly the arrival lags of both ends' influence.
